title: How to Play 13-Card Rummy: Complete Rules for Beginners
excerpt: The deal, jokers, sequences and sets, the pure sequence rule, declaring, drops and scoring: everything you need to play 13-card Indian rummy.
content:
**Short answer:** in 13-card rummy, each player gets 13 cards and tries to arrange all of them into valid groups. You need at least two sequences, and at least one of them must be a **pure sequence** with no joker. Each turn you draw one card and discard one. The first player to arrange all 13 cards correctly and declare wins the round.

This guide explains card-game rules for general knowledge. Online rummy played for money is prohibited in India under the Online Gaming Act, 2025; see our [online gaming laws guide](/blog/online-gaming-laws-in-india-what-players-should-know). 18+ only.

## What You Need

- **Players:** 2 to 6.
- **Cards:** usually two standard 52-card decks plus their printed jokers. Some two-player tables use a single deck.
- **Cards per player:** 13.

## The Deal and the Wild Joker

The dealer shuffles and deals 13 cards to each player, one at a time. One card is turned face up to start the **open pile** (the discard pile). The rest form the face-down **closed pile**.

One more card is drawn at random to choose the **wild joker**. Every card of that rank becomes a joker for the round, in all suits. The printed jokers from the decks are also jokers. Our guide to the [joker in rummy](/blog/joker-in-rummy-how-jokers-work) explains exactly what jokers can and cannot do.

## How a Turn Works

On your turn:

- **Draw** one card, either the top card of the closed pile or the top card of the open pile.
- **Discard** one card face up onto the open pile.

You always end your turn with 13 cards. Play moves clockwise.

## Valid Groups: Sequences and Sets

| Group | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Pure sequence | 3 or more consecutive cards of the same suit, with no joker used as a substitute | 5♥ 6♥ 7♥ |
| Impure sequence | 3 or more consecutive cards of the same suit, with a joker filling a gap | 5♥ Joker 7♥ |
| Set | 3 or 4 cards of the same rank in different suits (a joker may fill in) | 9♠ 9♦ 9♣ |

A few rules catch beginners out:

- An Ace can be low (A-2-3) or high (Q-K-A), but a sequence cannot wrap around (K-A-2 is not valid).
- A set cannot contain two cards of the same suit, even though two decks are in play.
- A set has at most 4 cards.

For more examples, see [rummy sequence rules](/blog/rummy-sequence-rules-pure-sequence-explained).

## The Winning Condition

To declare, all 13 cards must be in valid groups, and you must have:

- **at least two sequences**, and
- **at least one pure sequence** among them.

The remaining cards can be in further sequences or sets. When your hand is ready, draw your card, place your 14th card in the "finish" slot, and show your groups. If the groups are valid, you win the round.

## Drops

You can leave a round by **dropping**. In points rummy, dropping before your first draw usually costs 20 points (first drop), and dropping later costs 40 points (middle drop). Our guide on [when to drop in rummy](/blog/when-to-drop-in-rummy) covers the strategy.

## How Points Are Counted

When someone declares correctly, every other player scores points for the cards they have not grouped:

| Card | Points |
|---|---|
| Ace, King, Queen, Jack | 10 each |
| Number cards (2 to 10) | Face value |
| Jokers | 0 |

The maximum is usually 80 points. If a player has no pure sequence, all of their cards count, up to that cap. The winner scores 0. See [rummy points calculation](/blog/rummy-points-calculation) for worked examples.

## Common Formats

- **Points rummy:** one round, points decide the result.
- **Pool rummy (101 or 201):** players are eliminated when their total passes the limit. See [pool rummy rules](/blog/pool-rummy-rules-points-pool-deals).
- **Deals rummy:** a fixed number of deals, lowest total wins.
- **21-card rummy:** a larger hand with extra joker types. See [21-card rummy rules](/blog/21-card-rummy-rules-explained).

## Quick Tips for Your First Games

- Build your pure sequence first, before using jokers anywhere else.
- Discard high cards you are unlikely to use early, to limit your points if you lose.
- Watch what others pick up from the open pile; it shows what they are collecting.

More strategy is in [rummy tips for beginners](/blog/rummy-tips-for-beginners). House rules vary, so always check a table's rules before you play.
